data.narrative:
Citra Space Corporation is a Series A-stage space and aerospace company founded by Tom Nichols and Daniel Brunski, having raised $15M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparables universe of 5 public Space & Aerospace peers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private companies including SpaceX, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs.

Given data constraints, only the stage-progression method is reliably applicable. Using $15M in total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage transitions yields $30M. The peer-median approach cannot be applied: while 11 same-sector peers exist, none meet the minimum threshold of three comparables at identical or adjacent valuation stages. Public-comp anchoring is inapplicable because Citra's revenue figures are not disclosed—a standard limitation for private companies—preventing use of the 23.9x median P/S multiple observed across public Space & Aerospace names.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $26M to $34M, centered on $30M. Key uncertainties include the absence of a robust private-peer dataset at Citra's stage and valuation tier, lack of revenue or profitability data to benchmark against public multiples, and reliance on a single methodological pillar. This range should be stress-tested against capital efficiency metrics and pathway to Series B benchmarks as additional data becomes available.
